correctness.rationale: PASS: for compact full-dimensional K_i in R^{d_i}, m>=2, 1<=j<=n-1, the Minkowski polynomial of the Cartesian product factors exactly into factor volume polynomials. The established sharp Godbersen inequality bounds each factor coefficient q_{i,h} by binomial(d_i,h)^2; positivity gives the exact B_{d,j} bound. Simplices attain simultaneously. If any d_i>=2 factor is nonsimplex, the published interior strict equality theorem and h_i=max(1,j-(n-d_i)) produce a feasible strictly smaller coefficient summand, so equality forces all simplex factors. Dividing the convolution by binomial(n,j)^2 is exactly the self-collision probability of multivariate hypergeometric block counts; no missing normalization. For fixed m, d_i/n->alpha_i>0, j/n->beta in (0,1), uniform Stirling on n^{1/2+1/10} windows, exponential hypergeometric tails and the Gaussian determinant 1/prod(alpha_i) give n^{-(m-1)/2}[4*pi*beta*(1-beta)]^{-(m-1)/2}/sqrt(prod alpha_i). Independently checked 23 small coefficient polynomial/collision integer identities and limiting numerical direction. Critical published Godbersen inequality/equality is an explicit external premise, not reproved; finite checks do not prove the asymptotic or all-body inequality.
